anchored-split.description: A short panel that stays put on one side while the evidence for it scrolls past on the other - unequal columns, no photograph, and one claim held in view for as long as it takes to read the case for it.
anchored-split.needs: one claim the section is about, said in a title and at most two sentences - short enough to sit inside a phone-height panel and stay there. Then three or more real items that are the evidence for it, each with its own subheading and a paragraph from real material. Fewer than three and there is nothing to scroll past
anchored-split.summary: A panel that stays put on one side while the evidence for it scrolls past on the other.

announcement-bar.description: One short line and one link in a slim band above the site header, on the brand colour or the dark ground - an offer, a launch, a place newly served; the cheapest conversion lever a site has, and one line is all it holds.
announcement-bar.needs: one line of real news the brand can stand behind - an offer that exists, a place newly served, a date that is true - and the page it links to, which must exist. The bar's own name for assistive technology, two or three words
announcement-bar.summary: One line and a link above the site header, for the thing you most want visitors to know right now.

article-figure.description: One image in the flow of a written piece - a real figure with its caption and the credit inside that caption, running a little wider than the text column it sits between.
article-figure.needs: one real photograph that shows something the writing refers to, its own alt text describing what is in it, a caption saying what the reader is looking at and why it is here, and the credit the picture is licensed under. A picture that only fills space suits a pattern without a caption, since this one is built around what the caption says
article-figure.summary: One picture inside a piece of writing, with its caption and credit.

article-masthead.description: Bylined article header - metadata eyebrow over a hairline, display h1, a lede held to a short measure, and an author row under a second hairline.
article-masthead.needs: a real article title and a real lede of one or two sentences; the category the piece genuinely sits in; an honest read time and a genuine publication date; the name and role of the person who actually wrote it, and their real portrait with real alt text where the brand has one
article-masthead.summary: The top of a written piece: the title, who wrote it and when.

article-toc.description: In-page contents for a long piece - a short list of anchor links to the sections below, inside a native disclosure so a reader can put it away; with the behaviour library the link for the section being read is marked, and without it the list is the list.
article-toc.needs: the article's own section headings, in the order they appear, and an id written onto each of those headings in the body. The words in the list are the headings themselves, never a second set of titles written for the list
article-toc.summary: A short list of links to the sections of a long piece, which a reader can put away.

author-note.description: The block at the foot of a written piece - the writer's name, their standing, one paragraph of biography and an optional link to more of their work, on a panel that carries its weight without a portrait.
author-note.needs: the name of the person who actually wrote the piece and is willing to be named; what they do that bears on this subject - the job, the qualification, the years, the body they belong to; one paragraph of biography naming things a reader could go and check; and, where a page of their other work exists, a link to it
author-note.summary: The block at the end of a piece saying who wrote it and why they know the subject.

benefit-tiles.description: A run of two to six tall bordered tiles, each with a filled icon badge at the top and its title and copy set on the floor of the tile; the feature run for a page with no photography.
benefit-tiles.needs: two to six real capabilities the brand actually offers, each with a short title and one or two sentences of real copy; a simple line mark per tile, drawn inline so it takes the badge's ink; a label naming what the set is. Every claim here is a fact the brand can evidence: never a member number, a success rate, a superiority claim or an unqualified free without a source, and never that every profile is verified - verification on this platform is free and optional, so that one is untrue on every brand
benefit-tiles.summary: Two to six tall tiles, each with an icon and a short benefit.

capability-tabs.description: A topic switcher - a rail of pill tabs over one tinted panel pairing a claim, a ticked list of what is included and a half-panel image; with no behaviour library every panel renders stacked and readable.
capability-tabs.needs: two to five real capability stories the brand can stand behind, each with a short tab label, a claim heading, one or two sentences, three to five true points and its own photograph with alt text; a section heading and one supporting line
capability-tabs.summary: A row of tabs, each showing one feature in a panel below.

claim-stack.description: Three to five promises set very large, one to a screenful, separated by hairlines and nothing else - the section with nowhere to hide, for words the brand can stand behind.
claim-stack.needs: three to five claims the brand genuinely stands behind, each true, each said in about twelve words or fewer, and each carrying something the one above it did not. An optional line of plain support under any of them where a claim needs a condition stating. Nothing else - no figures, no photographs, no logos. Every claim here is a fact the brand can evidence: never a member number, a success rate, a superiority claim or an unqualified free without a source, and never that every profile is verified - verification on this platform is free and optional, so that one is untrue on every brand
claim-stack.summary: Three to five promises set very large, one to a screen.

colophon.description: The site footer a page carries itself - the brand's footer menu, the four legal links and a copyright line, set small on a quiet ground, centred on one line or laid out in columns, with the brand mark above them or not; the platform fills every link, the page owns the markup.
colophon.needs: the brand's name for the copyright line, and where the mark links to when it is shown. Every link on it is platform furniture
colophon.summary: Your site footer, with the menu, the legal links and the copyright line - on one line or in columns, with or without your logo.

comparison-table.description: A real table comparing three things against the same criteria - tier names across the top, one criterion per row, the recommended column named in words and never by colour alone.
comparison-table.needs: two or three real things the brand offers that are genuinely comparable against the same criteria, and the criteria themselves - one per row, in the brand's own words. Each cell says what that thing actually gives, not a tick borrowed from a competitor. A recommended column only where the brand recommends one
comparison-table.summary: Three things compared against the same list of criteria.

crumb-trail.description: The breadcrumb for a page below the site root - the root, the parents that exist and the current page as plain text, in one quiet line under the header, the separators hidden from assistive technology and the trail set to the page's container or to the article column.
crumb-trail.needs: the site root's relative path and its label, the label and relative path of each parent page that actually exists, and the current page's own title. A parent that has not been built is written as text, never linked
crumb-trail.summary: The short trail of links above a page that says where it sits in the site.

cta-assurance.description: The short run of reassurances that sits under a join control - what it costs, what is not being committed to, how long it takes - each one a fact the brand can evidence.
cta-assurance.needs: two to four things about signing up that are true and checkable - the price, whether a card is required, how long it takes, what is visible to whom. Each must be a fact the brand can evidence, never a promise about the future and never a time-limited offer. A bare free is not one - say what is free - and neither is verified members: verification on this platform is free and optional, so a line implying every member has it is untrue on every brand
cta-assurance.summary: The short run of reassurances that sits under a join button.

cta-band.description: Plain full-bleed closing call to action on a choice of four grounds - a centred claim, one supporting line and one control; the ordinary page finale, and the section most pages on a brand have in common.
cta-band.needs: a closing headline and one supporting line of real copy, both saying something the page has earned the right to say
cta-band.summary: A full-width closing band with one claim and one button.

cta-curtain.description: Full-viewport closing CTA pinned behind the last content section and uncovered as that section scrolls up and away, like a sheet being lifted.
cta-curtain.needs: a closing headline and one supporting line of real copy; the page's last content section, which becomes the covering sheet
cta-curtain.summary: A full-screen closing call to action, uncovered as the page above it scrolls away.

cta-image.description: Full-bleed photographic closing call to action - one landscape image, a scrim carrying the contrast, and a centred claim with both platform controls over it.
cta-image.needs: one landscape photograph strong enough to fill a band at least 2000px wide, with its own alt text and a CDN srcset ladder; a closing headline and one supporting line of real copy
cta-image.summary: A closing call to action over one full-width photograph.

cta-sticky.description: Mobile sticky bottom CTA bar - one join button always in the thumb zone on pages longer than two screens; hidden on desktop.
cta-sticky.needs: nothing beyond the page it sits on being longer than two mobile screens
cta-sticky.summary: A join button fixed to the bottom of the screen on a phone.

faq-details.description: Zero-JavaScript FAQ accordion on native details/summary - hairline rows, a plus that turns into a cross when the row opens.
faq-details.needs: the real questions people actually ask, each with a true answer in the brand's own words; a section heading
faq-details.summary: Common questions, each opening to its answer when tapped.

feature-panels.description: A run of full-bleed panels climbing a ground ladder - light, then the brand colour, then dark - each carrying a mark, a label, one large claim and a link on its floor.
feature-panels.needs: two to four real things the brand offers that genuinely sit in an order - tiers, levels, degrees of visibility. Three panels ship and there are exactly three grounds: for two, delete the middle panel; for four, repeat the middle ground rather than inventing a fourth. Each needs a short label, one claim of a few words, and a simple line mark drawn inline. A section heading, and a supporting line only where there is something true to say. Every claim here is a fact the brand can evidence: never a member number, a success rate, a superiority claim or an unqualified free without a source, and never that every profile is verified - verification on this platform is free and optional, so that one is untrue on every brand
feature-panels.summary: A run of full-width panels, each a shade stronger than the last.

gallery-scroll.description: User-driven horizontal gallery with CSS scroll-snap and no scroll bar; never auto-advances, gains previous and next controls when the behaviour library is on the page, and wraps into rows with scripting off.
gallery-scroll.needs: three or more real images of the same kind, each with real alt text, sized for the slot via the CDN
gallery-scroll.summary: A row of photographs you swipe sideways through.

heading-block.description: Section opener - rule-flanked eyebrow, tightly set display title, one supporting line; centred by default, left-aligned on phones.
heading-block.needs: a short eyebrow label, a title, and one supporting sentence - all real copy; the intro line is optional and deleted when there is nothing true to say
heading-block.summary: A heading and one supporting line, to introduce what follows.

hero-band.description: Inner-page opener - the page's h1 and one supporting line with a photograph beside them, or behind them on a panel of the ground, one band tall rather than a screen so the page's own content starts on the first screen.
hero-band.needs: one real photograph at least 1600px wide of people or a place the brand can show, with its own alt text; a headline for this page and one supporting sentence that says something the headline does not
hero-band.summary: A shorter opener for an inner page: the page's title and one line, beside or in front of a photograph.

hero-centred.description: Opener with the claim centred above a wide cropped photograph in its own band - the one hero that never lays a word over an image, so no scrim has to carry a ratio.
hero-centred.needs: a headline of one or two lines and one supporting sentence, both from real brand material; one landscape photograph at least 1600px wide with its own alt text and a CDN srcset ladder
hero-centred.summary: An opening claim centred above a wide photograph.

hero-overlay.description: Cinematic full-bleed opener - one photograph filling the first viewport, the claim and both platform controls set over a vignette scrim that dissolves into the page.
hero-overlay.needs: one landscape photograph strong enough to fill a whole screen, at least 2400px wide, with its own alt text and a CDN srcset ladder; a headline of one or two lines and one supporting sentence, both from real brand material
hero-overlay.summary: One photograph filling the first screen, with the claim over it.

hero-portrait.description: Conversion opener built to hold signup-card - one large portrait on one side, the headline, one line and the card on the other; the portrait rounded, arched or running to the page edge; on phones a short portrait strip, then the words, then the card.
hero-portrait.needs: one real photograph of a person or a couple, at least 1200px wide in portrait, that stands for the brand's members, with the person's OK - a named member, a testimonial's face or a founder reads better in a pattern built to name them - with its own alt text; a headline and one supporting sentence in the brand's own words; signup-card in place of the join button, or the button alone
hero-portrait.summary: An opener with one large portrait on one side, and the words and the sign-up card on the other.

hero-split.description: Conversion opener - value proposition on one side, one strong image on the other, single join CTA; stacks image-first on phones.
hero-split.needs: one hero image at least 1280px wide from real material, with its own alt text and a CDN srcset ladder; a headline and one-sentence subhead that state the actual offer
hero-split.summary: The opening claim on one side, a strong photograph on the other.

hero-squeeze.description: The whole page in one viewport - a photograph, one claim, one control, the reassurance under it and one piece of proof, with nothing below the fold at all.
hero-squeeze.needs: one landscape photograph at least 1600px wide with its own alt text; a headline of one line and one supporting sentence; and the two things that go under the control - the reassurance line, and one piece of real proof. Nothing else goes on the page, so everything the visitor needs to decide has to be in these five things
hero-squeeze.summary: The whole page in a single screen: a photograph, one claim, one button.

hero-stated.description: An opener made of words - a display claim, one supporting line and the join control - on a choice of three grounds and two alignments, with no photograph anywhere in it.
hero-stated.needs: a headline the brand can stand behind and one supporting sentence that says something the headline does not. Nothing else - no photograph, no figure, no logo. This is the opener for a brand that has words and nothing else yet. The headline is a fact the brand can evidence: never a member number, a success rate, a superiority claim or an unqualified free without a source, and never that every profile is verified - verification on this platform is free and optional
hero-stated.summary: An opener made of words rather than pictures.

key-takeaways.description: The summary box near the top of a piece - a heading and three to five one-line points a reader gets without reading the article, set as a quiet tinted block inside the writing rather than a card beside it.
key-takeaways.needs: three to five points, each a complete statement that stands on its own, each answerable from the article's own body, and none of them the title or the lede reworded. A point that only makes sense once the piece has been read is not a takeaway, and a point the article never supports belongs on neither
key-takeaways.summary: A short box near the top saying what the piece tells you.

link-cluster.description: A wrapping run of plain links to real pages - places, categories, topics - on a choice of three grounds, with no photograph, no figure and nothing to invent.
link-cluster.needs: real destination pages that already exist and already have content on them, and the brand's own name for each. Nothing else - no image, no copy, no figure. Every link must resolve: a cluster pointing at pages that are missing or empty is worse than no cluster, because it tells a reader the brand is bigger than it is
link-cluster.summary: A wrapping run of plain links to real pages: places, categories, topics.

listing-rows.description: Full-width ruled rows rather than a grid of cards - each row carries a linked title, a real sentence, and up to two true attributes aligned down their own columns; the index for a set of five or more things with no photograph between them.
listing-rows.needs: five or more real destinations or items of the same kind, each with the brand's own title, one true sentence about it, and at least one genuine attribute per row - a date, a category, a place, a count. Every link resolves to a page that already has content on it. An attribute column is deleted rather than filled with something invented
listing-rows.summary: Full-width rows rather than cards, each with a title and a line of detail.

masthead-nav.description: The site header the platform menu placeholder has no styling for - brand mark, the generated primary navigation and the login and join controls, on a choice of ground, two desktop arrangements, three small-screen behaviours, three answers for a menu too long for its row, a dropdown or a full-width panel for submenus, a bar that stays and shrinks as the page scrolls, a menu-free rung for a campaign page, three ways the mark meets its ground, a menu button with or without its word and its bars drawn four ways, and three bottom edges.
masthead-nav.needs: the brand's logo, the menu items configured on the platform, and three words in the brand's own language - one for the small-screen menu button, one for that same button while the menu is showing, and one for the item that holds whatever does not fit the row. Every other value on it is platform furniture
masthead-nav.summary: Your logo, the menu, and the log in and join buttons.

media-card-grid.description: A responsive grid of portrait image cards, each with a corner chip and its heading, one line of copy and an arrow cue set on a tuned bottom-up scrim over the photograph.
media-card-grid.needs: one real photograph per card, portrait-ish and at least 1280px wide, each with its own alt text; a short heading, one sentence of copy and a real destination URL per card; a short chip label per card only where the brand genuinely has one. Check that everyone whose face or words appear here has agreed to appear on a public page that anyone can reach without an account - consent to be a member is not consent to be marketing
media-card-grid.summary: A grid of upright cards, each led by a photograph.

member-filter.description: A row of pills switching between two or three live member blocks - one set per pill, each scoped differently by the platform, changed with a radio group and CSS alone so the page still carries no JavaScript.
member-filter.needs: two or three genuinely different member sets and the brand's own word for each pill, plus one word for what the pills do. A pill that shows the same members as the one beside it is a control that does nothing
member-filter.summary: Pills that switch between two or three sets of live members, with no script.

member-grid.description: A block of live members the platform fills at render time - the page ships an empty section and the CMS writes real profiles into it, so nothing here is authored, invented or kept in sync.
member-grid.needs: nothing from the partner, which is what makes this different from every other people pattern here - the platform supplies the members. What it does need is the location the block is scoped to, written exactly as the platform spells it, and the brand's own words for the two links and the empty state
member-grid.summary: Real members from your own site, filled in by the platform when the page is built.

member-strip.description: A short row of real members - photograph, name and one line each - sized to sit inside a hero or beside a control, so the proof is at the point of the ask rather than a screen away.
member-strip.needs: four to eight real members the brand can name, each with their real photograph and the name they actually use on the platform. Check that each of them has agreed to appear on a public page that anyone can reach without an account - consent to be a member is not consent to be marketing, and this is a face and a username on an acquisition page. It reads best with each face once, in the member's own photograph rather than stock; a member is never invented to lengthen the row
member-strip.summary: A short row of real members, with a photograph and a line each.

offer-split.description: A mid-page conversion beat with no photography in it - the argument set as prose on one side, the offer as a filled panel carrying its own heading and control on the other.
offer-split.needs: two or three short paragraphs making one argument, and a panel heading with one line saying plainly what is on offer. Everything here is words, so they have to be the brand's real ones
offer-split.summary: A conversion beat with no photography: the argument on one side, the offer on the other.

opener-split.description: Editorial section opener - a display title held to a short measure on the left, its supporting line pushed right and set to the title's baseline; stacks to one column on narrow screens.
opener-split.needs: a title, and one supporting sentence that says something the title does not; a short eyebrow label only where the section genuinely belongs to a named group
opener-split.summary: A title on the left with its supporting words on the right.

photo-band.description: A full-bleed photograph as a divider between two sections - no words on it or beside it, cover-cropped to one of three heights; the cheapest use of one good photograph, and the pause a long page needs between two runs of argument.
photo-band.needs: one real photograph at least 1600px wide that is worth looking at on its own, and alt text saying what is in it - or an empty alt where it is decoration only, which is the honest answer for most bands
photo-band.summary: One wide photograph across the page with no words on it, to give a long page a breath.

photo-cards.description: A run of cards with the photograph in its own box at the top and every word set below it on the card's own surface, so nothing is ever laid over an image.
photo-cards.needs: one real photograph per card with its own alt text; a short heading, one or two sentences and a real destination per card. Three or four cards read best
photo-cards.summary: Cards with the photograph on top and the words underneath.

picker-chips.description: The first sign-up decision as one tap - a question, a helper line, and a row of pill links that each go straight into the join flow.
picker-chips.needs: the real opening question the brand asks; two to four real options in the brand's own words; one helper line saying what picking does; and, where the question is who the visitor is or who they are looking for, the value each option sends to the join flow - the README lists them
picker-chips.summary: The first sign-up decision as one tap: a question and a row of choices.

pinned-cards.description: Full-screen photographic cards that pin as the page scrolls, each one sliding over the last like a dealt hand; pure CSS, and a plain stack of readable sections wherever it cannot pin.
pinned-cards.needs: one strong landscape photograph per card, at least 1600px wide, each with its own alt text; a short title and one or two sentences per card, in an order that means something. Two to four cards - a fifth stops being a hand and starts being a slideshow
pinned-cards.summary: Full-screen photo cards that stack over one another as you scroll.

portrait-prose.description: One person and their story - a portrait given a column of its own with a caption naming them, beside a heading and two or three paragraphs of prose on the page ground; the founder section, and the shape for any page that is really about one person.
portrait-prose.needs: one real portrait of a real person, with their OK to appear on a public page anyone can reach, at least 800px wide and taller than it is wide; their name and one line of standing for the caption; a heading; and two to four paragraphs of real prose in the brand's own voice about that person and why the brand exists
portrait-prose.summary: A photograph of a person given room of its own, beside their story in their own words.

portrait-wall.description: A lattice of member portraits three rows deep - three, five or seven columns across - with the strongest photograph held in the centre cell; a full-section image wall that carries scale rather than copy.
portrait-wall.needs: nine, fifteen or twenty-one different real member photographs, portrait-crop and at least 420px wide - each face once, and members' own photographs rather than stock, which reads as bought; a short label naming what the wall shows; and a section around it carrying the words, because the wall says nothing on its own. Check that everyone whose face or words appear here has agreed to appear on a public page that anyone can reach without an account - consent to be a member is not consent to be marketing
portrait-wall.summary: A lattice of member portraits with the strongest one held in the middle.

pricing-tiers.description: Two or three equal-height tier cards with aligned CTAs; the recommended tier named in words, never colour alone.
pricing-tiers.needs: the real tiers - names, real prices with currency, and each tier's actual features from brand material; a stated recommended tier or none
pricing-tiers.summary: Two or three plans side by side with matching buttons.

prose-column.description: The body of a piece of writing - one column held to a readable measure, with the headings, paragraphs, lists and quotes an article actually uses already set.
prose-column.needs: real writing. Headings that say what their section contains, each section opening with a complete one-sentence answer to the question its heading raises
prose-column.summary: The body of a written piece, held to a readable width.

pull-quote.description: A line lifted out of the running text and set large between two runs of body copy - the article's own words, repeated for emphasis, with no attribution and no ask.
pull-quote.needs: one sentence taken word for word from the body copy on the same page, short enough to read in one glance, and carrying an idea rather than a fact. It is repetition on purpose: the line must already be somewhere above or below it, and shortening it to fit means shortening the sentence in the body too
pull-quote.summary: One line from the article, set large to break up a long read.

quote-feature.description: One oversized testimonial on a full-width tinted stage - eyebrow pinned to the stage, display-size quote held to a short measure, circular portrait and attribution beneath.
quote-feature.needs: one real testimonial, quoted word for word as the person actually wrote it, with their real name and a true attribution line; one real portrait of that person with real alt text; a star rating only where a real published rating exists. A quote nobody said is not a candidate for this pattern - do not write one, do not paraphrase one, and do not attach a name to praise that arrived unattributed. Check that everyone whose face or words appear here has agreed to appear on a public page that anyone can reach without an account - consent to be a member is not consent to be marketing
quote-feature.summary: One oversized testimonial on a full-width tinted stage.

quote-image.description: One real quote at display size over a full-width photograph - the words on a soft-edged shade of the scrim that carries their contrast, placed in the middle, on the left or on the right, with the rest of the photograph clear or evenly darkened.
quote-image.needs: one real quote, word for word, from a member's review the platform returns or from material the brand gives, with the name it came with and a true detail line; one landscape photograph at least 2000px wide with its own alt text - a place, or people who stand for the brand, reads best behind a quote, where a face tends to read as the speaker's
quote-image.summary: One real quote, set large over a full-width photograph.

rating-mark.description: A published rating shown as whole stars beside the figure itself - the stars are the glance, the text is the claim, and only the text is read out.
rating-mark.needs: a rating the platform actually publishes, with the number of ratings behind it. Both are facts with a source - a score with no count is unreadable as evidence, and a score the brand cannot point at is invented proof
rating-mark.summary: A published rating shown as whole stars beside the figure.

safety-protections.description: Categorised safety protections as cards, each carrying three registers - the name of the protection, what it does, and the line the reader takes away about how it protects them.
safety-protections.needs: real protections the brand actually operates, each with the name it is known by, one or two plain sentences of what it does, and one sentence saying what that means for the reader; a section heading. Nothing here may be invented - a protection written because it sounds right is a promise about someone's physical safety that nobody is keeping
safety-protections.summary: Safety measures as cards, grouped by what they protect against.

scene-cards.description: Places, events or ideas as big photo cards - one large and two small, or three equal - each photograph with its name under it or across its foot and where or when in italics. The twin of story-cards, the same card for a brand with no couples' stories to show.
scene-cards.needs: three real things the brand is about - a place members meet, an event it runs, an idea for a date - each with a photograph at least 1200px wide in portrait or the library's placeholder, its name, and where or when it is. A couple's story reads best in story-cards
scene-cards.summary: Big photo cards for the places, events and ideas the brand is about.

signup-card.description: Conversion card for an opener - set in place of the join button in hero-overlay, hero-split, hero-stated, hero-squeeze or hero-portrait, it asks who the visitor is, who they are looking for, their date of birth and their email, then hands everything to the brand's own join flow pre-filled. The opener keeps its own headline and picture; on a wide screen it sets the words on one side and the card on the other.
signup-card.needs: an opener to sit in (hero-overlay, hero-split, hero-stated, hero-squeeze or hero-portrait); the card's title; the brand's wording for each answer; the brand's interest labels for the two choice steps, spelled exactly as its join flow spells them, with the two questions and the first-name label; the consent sentence HubPeople supplies, with the brand's terms and privacy links; one line saying the password is chosen on the next screen; the brand's platform, because only Excite brands offer couples
signup-card.summary: A short sign-up card that sits in an opener in place of its join button.

signup-steps.description: Conversion opener - a headline beside a short sign-up card that asks who the visitor is, who they are looking for, their date of birth and their email, then hands everything to the brand's own join flow pre-filled; stacks card-under-headline on phones.
signup-steps.needs: a headline and one supporting sentence in the brand's own words; the card's title; the brand's wording for each answer; the brand's interest labels for the two choice steps, spelled exactly as its join flow spells them, with the two questions and the first-name label; the consent sentence HubPeople supplies, with the brand's terms and privacy links; one line saying the password is chosen on the next screen; the brand's platform, because only Excite brands offer couples
signup-steps.summary: An opening that asks the first sign-up questions on the page itself.

source-note.description: The line under a claim saying where it came from - who measured it, what they counted, and when - placeable under any figure, statement, answer or card.
source-note.needs: for the claim it sits under - who produced the figure, one phrase saying what it counts, and when it was measured. All three, in that order. A figure whose source cannot be named does not get this component; it comes off the page
source-note.summary: The line under a claim saying where the figure came from.

stat-rows.description: Full-width editorial statistic rows - a large figure, a hairline that draws itself across, one supporting sentence set against it on the right.
stat-rows.needs: each real statistic exactly as the brand publishes it, one supporting sentence per figure from real material, and a short label naming what the strip is
stat-rows.summary: Full-width rows, each a large figure with a line explaining it.

stats-band.description: Full-bleed inverted proof band - a hairline lattice of real figures, each one paired with its label in a definition list; renders complete with no script.
stats-band.needs: an eyebrow, a short band title, and the real figures with their labels - every number taken from brand material and written into the markup as text, never computed on the page
stats-band.summary: A full-width band of real figures, each paired with what it means.

steps-numbered.description: How-it-works steps as full-bleed image cards - a giant counter numeral and the step copy set on a dark bottom-up scrim over photography.
steps-numbered.needs: one real photograph per step, portrait-ish and at least 1020px wide, each with its own alt text; a short step title and one sentence of body copy per step, in the real order they happen
steps-numbered.summary: How it works, as numbered image cards.

steps-plain.description: How-it-works steps as a hairline lattice of text cells - a counter numeral, a title and a line of copy per step, with no photography anywhere in it.
steps-plain.needs: three to five real steps in the order they actually happen, each with a short title and one or two sentences; a section heading. It carries no photography - that is the point of it
steps-plain.summary: How it works, as a plain numbered lattice with no photographs.

story-cards.description: Couples' stories as big photo cards - one large and two small, or three equal - each photograph with the couple's names under it or across its foot and where they are in italics. The twin of scene-cards, which carries places, events and ideas in the same card for a brand with no couples' stories to show.
story-cards.needs: three couples who met through the brand, each with their own photograph at least 1200px wide in portrait, the names they are happy to be shown by, where they are, and a line in their own words where they gave one. Works best with each couple's OK to appear on a public page anyone can reach; a brand with no couples' stories has the same card for places, events and ideas in scene-cards
story-cards.summary: Big photo cards for couples who met here: each photograph, their names and where they are.

testimonial-carousel.description: Reader-driven testimonial carousel on a radio group - one card centre stage, its neighbours peeking at reduced scale, nothing that moves on its own, and previous and next controls when the behaviour library is on the page.
testimonial-carousel.needs: at least three real testimonials - each quote as the person actually wrote it, with a real name and a true attribution line; one real portrait per person with real alt text; a section heading; each quote short enough to read in about three lines, since the longest in the set sets the height of every slide. Check that everyone whose face or words appear here has agreed to appear on a public page that anyone can reach without an account - consent to be a member is not consent to be marketing
testimonial-carousel.summary: Testimonials you move through one at a time.

testimonial-grid.description: Three equal-height testimonial cards with portraits overlapping the card edge; one card may be filled and is named as featured in words.
testimonial-grid.needs: three real testimonials - each quote as the person actually wrote it, their name, and their attribution; one real portrait per person with real alt text; a public source URL only where the testimonial genuinely has one. Check that everyone whose face or words appear here has agreed to appear on a public page that anyone can reach without an account - consent to be a member is not consent to be marketing
testimonial-grid.summary: Three testimonial cards side by side, with portraits.

trust-row.description: Hairline-bracketed strip of assurance marks - a membership lockup beside a row of icon-over-label compliance badges, answering whether the brand is legitimate at the point of sign-up.
trust-row.needs: real, verifiable compliance marks or memberships the brand actually holds and nothing else - the supplied membership logo file with its real alt text, the association's real name, the real membership status, and the real name of each certification or regulation the brand can evidence
trust-row.summary: A strip of assurance marks: a membership lockup and a row of guarantees.

zigzag-rows.description: Alternating image-and-copy rows down the middle of a page - the image side swaps row to row through an explicit modifier class, and only the image ever moves.
zigzag-rows.needs: one real photograph per row, at least 1000px on the short side, each with its own alt text; a short heading and one or two sentences per row; optionally one destination link per row
zigzag-rows.summary: Image-and-words rows where the image swaps side row to row.
